newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, July clings to support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, July clings to support.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures mostly ended lower Thursday in a thin session, with mild weather and a soft physical market almost pressuring the market through support, industry sources said.
Spot-July skidded 6.6 cents to close at $2.25 per million British thermal units. August settled six cents lower at $2.251. Most other months ended steady to down 5.6 cents.

"We couldn't get above unchanged, so they sold it off. We could head a little further south before people step up and buy it. July needs to hold $2.18," said one Midwest trader, adding mild weather could pressure the early-June cash.

Most traders agreed early-June forecasts calling for normal to slightly below-normal Midwest and Northeast weather could make it difficult for the bulls near-term though some Southwest heat and injection demand may limit the slide.

And chart traders said the technical picture was looking shaky after July's brief dip today below the trendline. The $2.25 July close just held the line and traders said a likely soft weekend cash market tomorrow could push it through. Next support was seen at $2.17-2.18, with further buying likely in the $2.09 area. Resistance was still at $2.37-2.38 and then at the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, June Gulf Coast prices lost more than a nickel Thursday to the mid-to-high $2.20s. June Midcon gas slipped a similar amount to about $2.10. New York city gate June gas tumbled more than a dime to about $2.50.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip skidded 6.6 cents to $2.255. NYMEX said 30,255 contracts traded, less than half of Wednesday's revised tally of 77,374.

On KCBT, July finished 3.8 cents lower at $2.107, while deferreds ended down by 3.5 to 4.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.8 cents to 14.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 140 lots traded, down sharply from Wednesday's total of 248.
